parole.testo: From the Norman/Picard dialect, from Old Northern French, equivalent to the Old French caboce. Compare the English cabbage ultimately of the same origin. Compare also Italian caboccia, capoccia, Spanish cabeza, possibly ultimately from a derivative Latin caput.

parole.significato: in a homely manner, without ceremony, informally
parole.testo: [mid-18th century] Derived from Norman or Picard franc (“frank”). The original meaning of à la franquette was "frankly" (franchement), "sincerely" (sincèrement).
